title: arXiv mathematics — notable papers in the 6 October 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: This is an inferred, scope-based selection, not an official arXiv trending chart. Citation evidence for these recent preprints is sparse; the ordering does not measure readership or popularity. All mathematical results are author claims in preprints and their proofs have not been independently verified here.

sections.title: Presenting a proof of the Kannan-Lovasz-Simonovits conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors say they prove a dimension-free Poincare inequality for isotropic log-concave probability measures, using a criterion based on high-order derivatives of tilt averages.
sections.claimed_result: A universal constant bounds the Poincare constant of every isotropic log-concave probability measure, independent of dimension.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Probability measures on Euclidean space that are log-concave and isotropically normalized.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem states existence of a universal constant without giving an explicit numerical value. The authors acknowledge that ChatGPT found most proof ideas; the proof needs independent expert checking.

sections.title: A Proof of the Linear Hadwiger Conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors claim an absolute-constant linear upper bound on the chromatic number of graphs with no K_t minor, and say GPT-6 Astra found the proof following their directions.
sections.claimed_result: Every graph has chromatic number at most an absolute constant times its Hadwiger number.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite graphs, with chromatic number bounded in terms of the largest complete-graph minor.
sections.unique_caveat: This is the linear Hadwiger conjecture, not the stronger classical bound chi(G) <= h(G), which the introduction says remains unresolved. The AI-generated argument needs independent checking.

sections.title: The LeBrun--Salamon conjecture is true in dimension up to 56
sections.abstract: The authors claim the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture for positive quaternionic Kahler manifolds through quaternionic dimension 14, using isometry-group bounds and characteristic-number inequalities.
sections.claimed_result: The conjecture is proved for positive quaternionic Kahler manifolds of quaternionic dimension n <= 14 (real dimension at most 56).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Positive quaternionic Kahler manifolds, within quaternionic dimension n <= 14.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated result stops at quaternionic dimension 14 and does not settle higher dimensions.

sections.title: The Prym-Green conjecture in even genera up to 30
sections.abstract: The authors claim the Prym-Green conjecture for every even genus from 20 through 30, using cyclic-symmetry degenerations and finite-field rank computations.
sections.claimed_result: The conjecture is asserted for even genera 20--30 by decomposing a Koszul differential into character-indexed maps and computing their ranks over finite fields.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Prym-canonical curve syzygies in the stated even genera.
sections.unique_caveat: The result covers only genera 20--30; the finite-field computation has not been independently replayed here.

sections.title: The linear independence of 1, zeta(3), and zeta(4)
sections.abstract: The author claims that 1, zeta(3), and zeta(4) are linearly independent over the rationals, using a determinant method and simultaneous zeta-value approximations.
sections.claimed_result: Linear independence over Q of the triple 1, zeta(3), zeta(4).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Rational linear relations among the three specified real constants; not a claim of algebraic independence.
sections.unique_caveat: The result concerns one specific triple and does not establish broader algebraic-independence conjectures.

sections.title: A sharp Merino--Welsh-type inequality for matroids
sections.abstract: The authors claim the conjectured optimal constant c*=x0 in a Tutte-polynomial inequality for finite loopless, coloopless matroids, with x0 approximately 2.22668.
sections.claimed_result: For the specified inequality over loopless, coloopless finite matroids, the minimal constant is x0, the largest real root of x^3-9(x-1).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite matroids without loops or coloops, and the stated Tutte-polynomial inequality.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not claim extensions to matroids with loops or coloops or to other related inequalities.

sections.title: Chowla Conjecture for the truncated Mobius function over F_q[t]
sections.abstract: The author claims an analytic proof of the two-point Chowla conjecture for truncated Mobius values in the fixed-q function-field setting, using a bivariate Erdos-Kac theorem and a Brun sieve.
sections.claimed_result: The two-point Chowla statement for the truncated Mobius function over F_q[t] with q fixed.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Function fields over a fixed finite field; the observable is truncated Mobius and the result is two-point.
sections.unique_caveat: This does not establish the integer version of Chowla or higher-point correlations and is restricted to fixed q.

sections.title: Large corank of dense random regular digraphs
sections.abstract: The authors give an exponentially small upper bound on the probability that the adjacency matrix of a uniformly random dense regular digraph has corank at least k.
sections.claimed_result: For fixed 0<lambda<=1/2 and degree lambda n <= d <= (1-lambda)n, the claimed bound is P[rank(A)<=n-k] <= 2 exp(-c_lambda k n), for 1<=k<=n.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Uniform random d-regular directed graphs in the dense degree range; the constant depends only on lambda.
sections.unique_caveat: The bound does not address sparse degree regimes outside the stated dense interval.
